listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Friday, October 16, 2026. The lead story is a shooting at a primary school in Oregon. Police say three children and a teacher were killed. The victims were aged 5, 8 and 11. Police say a 16-year-old suspect opened fire in the city of Bend. An armed bystander shot the suspect dead after he followed him into the school. Now, the front stories. Ukrainian drones struck a refinery in Russia's Ryazan region, after Zelenskyy said a brief truce spurned by Moscow was over. Kimberly Guilfoyle resigned as U.S. ambassador to Greece, after the White House asked for her resignation over alleged improper conduct. The FBI and the Postal Inspection Service are investigating suspicious mailings sent to election officials and congressional offices. BBC Verify counted 12 vessels struck in a week near Hormuz, a record high. Now, the sections. In technology and AI, Anthropic's Compliance API now returns saved instructions for Enterprise organizations, in beta. In politics, The Lever reports nearly 430 million dollars spent against taxing the rich. In world news, the Brewers swept the Dodgers and reach the World Series for the first time since 1982. In sports, the 49ers may get a returning receiver in Week 6. In Atlanta, Invest Atlanta approved a 330 million dollar bond for Amsterdam Walk. In architecture, Lion Green Road won the RIBA Stirling Prize. In science, NASA is tracking a historic El Niño this fall. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Three children and teacher killed in US primary school shooting
lead.note: A shooting at a primary school in Oregon killed three children and a teacher, according to BBC World reporting. The suspect was shot dead by an armed bystander who followed him into the school, police said. A BBC report on the attack gives more detail on how the shooting unfolded in Bend, where local police say a 16-year-old suspect opened fire. The victims were aged 5, 8 and 11, along with a teacher. Police have described the bystander's actions in the incident. The story is a reminder of the human cost of gun violence in American schools. Coverage continues as investigators work to establish the events of the day.
